messages:
Maya: Heads up — started seeing a p95/p99 latency jump for text-gen in us-west2 A10 pool right after the canary of dynamic-kernel-picker rolled at 10:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/series/ux321 (screenshot)

Maya: p95 went from ~120ms -> 320ms, p99 from ~420ms -> 1.6s. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% at the same time.

jared: ugh. any CI alerts? did the rollout include batching changes?

priya: CI perf did show a small regression on e2e-latency job for a10 targets, but it was marked as flaky and auto-ack'd. I started a manual perf job just now (run 2027-06-03-12).

lucas: dynamic-kernel-picker PR (merge 4321) touched kernel selection + batching heuristics. It tries to pick nvcc-optimized kernels for large seqs and fall back to fallback kernels on contention. Could be choosing the wrong path under A10 memory pressure.

sasha: infra metrics show increased rx_errors on several A10 NICs around 10:11-10:15. Packet drops could cause retransmit stalls that amplify tail latency.

infra-bot: deploy-logs: canary/dynamic-kernel-picker - merged by lucas at 2027-06-03T10:09:14Z -> started rollout to us-west2-a10. Instances updated: 28/28.

Maya: I captured a short profiler trace from a single A10 host that had the spike. attaching snippet:

```
[2027-06-03T10:14:03Z] select_kernel: chosen=fast_gemm_v2 seq=1024 mem_avail=2.1GB
[2027-06-03T10:14:03Z] kv_cache: lookup miss rate=0.24 (baseline ~0.05)
[2027-06-03T10:14:03Z] fallback: switching kernel -> fallback_gemm_cpu after 180ms busy-wait
[2027-06-03T10:14:03Z] net: tx_retransmits=73 rx_errors=9
[2027-06-03T10:14:04Z] rpc: downstream retry due to ECONNRESET
```

jared: that looks like two orthogonal issues glueing together: NIC flakiness causing RPC retries -> kv cache churn -> kernel picker misreads memory/latency signal and falls back to CPU path, which kills tail.

priya: started a bisect across merges between 4321 and the previous stable. early result points to the kernel-picker heuristics change in 4321 as necessary but not sufficient. When I force network emulation to drop packets in staging, we reproduce the tail regardless of batching tweaks.

lucas: interesting — so the picker probably uses a latency probe that assumes low network jitter. If probes timeout due to retransmits it ramps to conservative kernels. We never tested that failure mode on A10 with smaller NIC buffers.

sasha: ops also saw elevated interrupt CPU on a subset of A10 machines -> kernel preemption + IRQ storms. I opened ticket #OPS-998 to check NIC driver version and offload settings.

Maya: mitigation options? I can pin us-west2 A10 pool to legacy-kernel-picker for now or roll back the merge. Thoughts?

jared: pin the picker config per-pool — that's fastest and lower blast radius. Rollback if pin doesn't help.

priya: I'll apply per-pool config to force "picker.mode=legacy" on prod us-west2-a10 and run perf job. ETA 20m.

infra-bot: config-change: runtime.picker.mode=legacy applied to pool:us-west2-a10 by priya at 2027-06-03T10:45:02Z

oncall-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2027-0612-A10-KVTAIL (sev3) — owner: jared.

Maya: after pin, p95 back down to ~130ms and p99 ~460ms in the next 10m window. KV hit-rate recovered to baseline. Looks like pin worked as mitigation.

lucas: still want to follow up: add probe resilience to kernel-picker (tolerance to transient network errors), and add explicit NIC metrics gating in rollout. I'll open PR to add hysteresis and probe retries.

priya: action items: 1) keep picker pinned in us-west2-a10 until PR with network-hardened picker merges (priya) 2) ops to audit NIC drivers and interrupt settings (sasha) 3) add e2e perf test with induced packet loss for A10 pools (jared + lucas).

Maya: thanks all — marking rollout on hold for other regions until we validate. :thumbsup:

jared: I'll own postmortem and link perf artifacts. If anyone has raw perf traces, drop in #eng-runtime/artifacts.

Maya: attaching small trace tarball to artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/incident-1823456789/trace.tar.gz

sasha: noted. OPS will upgrade nic-driver on a cohort of A10 hosts and monitor.

priya: closing bisect — root cause: picker heuristics too sensitive to transient network-induced latency -> triggered conservative kernel fallback that amplifies tail. Repro: emulate packet drops + low memory -> p99 spike.

Maya: final status: mitigation applied (picker pinned), escalation to SEV3, follow-ups assigned. Will draft short blurb for all-hands.
